g1-implement.title: G1 (validate the zero-fit throttle-anchored burn-rate hypothesis, NOT wired): implement
g1-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md for this gate. Task: (1) Add a cited per-season FIA fuel-regulation table (flow-rate cap kg/h and max race-start fuel kg: flow 100 kg/h flat 2014-2025, ~70 kg/h-equivalent from 2026 per the energy-based 3000 MJ/h limit; max fuel 110kg 2019-2025, 70kg 2026 — sources recorded in MISSION_FRAME.md Governing Constraints). (2) Build src/physics/burn_rate_calibration.py implementing the ZERO-FIT estimator: for each race ('R') session, reuse the existing single seam `src.data.telemetry_session.build_db_session(TelemetryStore().read_session(year, gp_name, 'R'))` (car_data keyed by driver -> DataFrame with `Throttle` (0-100) + `SessionTime` timedelta; `DBSession.laps` -> `_ShimLaps` with `Driver`/`LapNumber`/`LapStartTime`/`Time`); for each lap, time-weight-average throttle over [LapStartTime, Time) and estimate `lap_burn_kg = flow_rate_cap_kg_per_s * mean_throttle_fraction * lap_duration_s`. Average per season (NO cross-season pooling; each season fully independent). (3) Cross-check across a WIDER circuit range, not just the two free-flow anchors (human steer: 'those were helpful for fitting, let's check a range of races') — Bahrain, Spain (2026: 'Barcelona-Catalunya', since Bahrain is absent from the 2026 calendar and the DB names 2026's Spain round differently), Silverstone (moderate/in-between case, matches the circuit set already used in the uncommitted scripts/mass_validation_dashboard.py panel C), and Monaco (heavily pace-managed adversarial case). At EACH circuit, compare the throttle-integral estimate against the INDEPENDENT lap-time-slope signal (OLS observed lap-time-vs-lap-number slope vs the mass model's predicted slope at the throttle-derived kg/lap), reporting real numbers per (season, circuit). Expected pattern to report explicitly: agreement at Bahrain/Spain/Silverstone (both methods should roughly concur); at Monaco, the lap-time-slope signal is expected to diverge (known pace-management confound) while the throttle-integral estimate should stay physically sane and duration-adjusted-comparable to the other circuits — that divergence pattern, if observed, is evidence FOR the throttle method's robustness, not a failure of it. Do not average/pool the per-circuit comparisons into one number; report per (season, circuit). (4) SC/VSC natural-reproduction check: using the same telemetry, compute the throttle-integral burn estimate separately for SC/VSC-flagged laps vs green-flag laps within the same sessions (join lap_times.track_status from the season DB, or the store's own status if present) and report the ratio — check how it compares to the existing hardcoded SC_BURN_FRACTION=0.5 (informational only; do not change SC_BURN_FRACTION). (5) Add a runnable script (e.g. scripts/validate_burn_rate_hypothesis.py) that prints/plots this evidence for 2019-2026. Do NOT modify mass_model.py's public constants and do NOT wire anything into race_mass/fuel_at_lap in this gate — that is explicitly deferred to a follow-up decided after this evidence is reviewed. Dispatch a subagent invoking constellation-implementer with the completed handoff. Wait for and integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT as evidence.

g1-review.title: G1: review
g1-review.imperative: Fill templates/REVIEWER_HANDOFF.template.md: verify the estimator is genuinely zero-fit (flow_rate_cap is a literal cited constant, not derived via regression), verify each season/circuit combination (both the throttle-integral estimate and the lap-time-slope cross-check) is computed independently with no pooling across seasons OR circuits, verify the cross-check actually covers Bahrain, Spain (or Barcelona-Catalunya for 2026), Silverstone, AND Monaco (not just the original two anchors), verify the reported Monaco divergence is explained as an expected pace-management confound rather than hand-waved, verify it reuses the existing build_db_session/TelemetryStore seam rather than a parallel loader, verify the regulation citations are present and accurate, verify mass_model.py is untouched (read-only) and SC_BURN_FRACTION is unchanged, verify the cross-check and SC/VSC evidence are reported with actual numbers per (season, circuit) — not just asserted. Dispatch a subagent invoking constellation-reviewer with the completed handoff. Wait for and integrate the returned REVIEW_RESULT as evidence.

anchors.inherits: g1-implement anchors — review verifies the change against the same structural/capability/constraint/decision/evidence anchors

g1-integrate.title: G1: integrate
g1-integrate.imperative: Check the REVIEW_RESULT verdict. APPROVE: run the verification command, confirm postconditions pass, advance this gate. BLOCK: send the implementer back for rework or raise a blocker if the gate is unresolvable. Log any out-of-scope finds as triage candidates (e.g. the deferred wiring work itself, once this evidence is reviewed, becomes a triage/follow-up candidate at the triage step).
